headlines.text: It was 2024 when a new champion was crowned for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as Jon Moxley vs. Bryan Danielson battled it out, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 8.59 ? an outstanding performance from both sides ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. In a match that also ended Bryan Danielson's full-time in-ring career, Moxley choked him unconscious with the Bulldog Choke to become a four-time AEW World Champion, with the Death Riders finishing the beatdown by pulling a plastic bag over his head.

2022 brought us this moment: a new champion was crowned for the AEW All-Atlantic Title as Orange Cassidy vs. PAC battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.86 ? a well-worked match ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. PAC reached for a ring-bell hammer but was foiled by Danhausen's interference, letting Cassidy land back-to-back Orange Punches to finally beat PAC and win his first AEW singles title.

2024 brought us this moment: the AEW International Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Konosuke Takeshita vs. Ricochet vs. Will Ospreay battled it out, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 9.13 ? an incredible outing ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. Fletcher's screwdriver stab to Ospreay's head set up Takeshita's knee strike to win the AEW International Championship, ending Ospreay's second reign at 48 days.

secondaries.text: On this day in 2024, the AEW World Tag Team Titles was up for grabs as The Young Bucks vs. Private Party went to war, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 6.89.
Flash back to 2022, when Luchasaurus made their return to AEW television after 4 months away, appearing on Dynamite.
On a Saturday in 2024, back when Mariah May vs. Willow Nightingale clashed for the AEW Women's World Title, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 7.34 ? a good, competitive contest.
